text:
hana_sales: FYI demo stalled. Client received garbled SSE chunks then stream closed. Happened ~90s into a long reply. Can we triage before the follow-up call?

demo_agent: (system) client: acme-embed-03, req: req_a1b2, endpoint: /v1/generate/stream, region: us-east-1

diego_se: Do we have the raw event stream from the client? Need to see whether `\n\n` boundaries were preserved or chunks were reordered.

demo_agent: Snippet (sanitized): ```
data: {"idx":1,"text":"Part A"}
data: {"idx":2,"text":"Part B"}
data: {"idx":3,"text":"Par`"
```

sam_runtime: That backtick suggests the client cut mid-UTF8 codepoint. Runtime shows successful flushes of all parts, then a FIN from client IP 198.51.100. No server-side error. Could be an intermediary re-chunking or the browser's event parser hitting a partial UTF-8 boundary.

alex_support: Common in embed/webview combos. Two quick asks: 1) ask client to capture raw bytes via curl -N from their network to rule out CDN; 2) try a polyfilled EventSource or fetch+ReadableStream to see if parsing differs.

diego_se: Also check whether the customer's BFF (edge backend-for-frontend) is concatenating multiple SSE responses. If the BFF does a naive string join it can reorder frames under concurrency. Recommend adding `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and avoiding server-side response buffering.

hana_sales: Can we push a runtime canary that emits small keepalive comments and forces flush boundaries? Demo in 25m.

sam_runtime: I can enable a canary that flushes every 8KB or every 8s and emits `:ka` comments. ETA 15m; will post canary URL and `X-CANARY: sse-fix` header.

diego_se: Client-side safe parser snippet to share with ACME: ```
let acc='';
source.onmessage = e => { acc += e.data; try{ const obj = JSON.parse(acc); acc=''; handle(obj); }catch(err){ /* wait for more chunks */ } }
```
Also recommend using TextDecoder when using fetch streams to avoid splitting codepoints.

alex_support: If curl shows clean frames but browser shows truncation, ask them to test in Chrome desktop to rule out mobile/webview quirks. Also capture any middlebox (Cloudflare/ALB) headers.

hana_sales: Great. I'll send instructions and ask them to bypass CDN temporarily. Please drop the canary URL when ready. Thanks! :thumbsup:
